poster_title: MLP Memory: A Retriever-Pretrained Memory for Large Language Models
authors: Rubin Wei, Jiaqi Cao, Jiarui Wang, Jushi Kai, Qipeng Guo, Bowen Zhou, Zhouhan Lin

content: Decoder-only LLMs excel in tasks but face challenges in knowledge utilization and factual accuracy.
RAG and similar methods offer flexible knowledge access but suffer from high inference latency.
CPT and LoRA are computationally efficient but risk catastrophic forgetting and degrade general performance.
Trade-off between flexible external knowledge access and efficient inference in LLMs.
Need for a method that internalizes retrieval patterns without explicit document access.
Challenge of maintaining model performance and reducing hallucinations while improving inference speed.
Propose MLP Memory, a lightweight parametric module pretrained to imitate a kNN retriever's behavior.
Integrate MLP Memory with Transformer decoders through probability interpolation.
Achieve end-to-end differentiability, highly compressible memory, low inference-time latency, scalable general knowledge memorization, and long-term memory.
Evaluated on WikiText-103 and Web datasets.
Tested on five QA benchmarks and nine general NLP tasks.
Compared inference efficiency and accuracy with RAG and kNN-LM methods.

content: 17.5% and 24.1% scaling gains on WikiText-103 and Web datasets.
12.3% relative improvement on five QA benchmarks and 5.2 points absolute gain across nine NLP tasks.
Reduced hallucinations by up to 10 points on HaluEval.
panels.figure_caption: Performance and efficiency comparison with other methods.

content: MLP Memory bridges the gap between efficient inference and effective knowledge access in LLMs.
Offers a practical alternative to RAG and fine-tuning approaches, providing better accuracy and faster inference.
